results.title: Tariffs send shockwaves through Georgia's industries
results.content:
The White House initially established 10% tariffs on imports from all countries, along with higher “reciprocal” tariffs targeting nations such as China, Vietnam and members of the European Union that levy tariffs on U.S. goods. Mexico and Canada — Georgia’s top export destinations — were spared from the new tariffs. [...] In 2024, the Peach State ranked seventh nationwide in net exports, shipping around $53.1 billion in locally made products overseas while importing about $145.6 billion, according to the Georgia Chamber of Commerce.

President Donald Trump’s newly unveiled tariffs have sent shockwaves through the manufacturing, technology and agricultural sectors across the country — particularly in Georgia. [...] “I don’t think there’s any question that these tariffs are going to impact Georgia,” Safavian told _State Affairs_. “There’s not a single vehicle sold in the U.S. market that is made from 100% domestic parts.”

results.title: The global supply chain's reaction to the Trump tariffs
results.content: Already, some companies are significantly re-evaluating their processes and making significant changes to their supply chain strategies, Wenck observes, but not necessarily by moving production to the United States as is the stated goal of the Trump Administration. For instance, Wenck relates the story of a client that previously imported goods into the US and then distributed them to Canada. In response to the new tariffs, they are reorganizing their supply chain to import directly into [...] “A supply chain is a never-ending loop, right? That's the purpose of the supply chain, and anybody who wants to improve their supply chain is really looking to better forecast the demand and then plan inventory to it,” explains Wenck. “The tariff activity impacts forecast accuracy, leading companies to pause or cancel orders and beg or plead with vendors.” [...] Foremost, the global supply chain is experiencing a moment of immense distress as multiple factors work to disrupt it on both a short- and medium-term perspective. Most immediately, tariffs have disrupted the accuracy of demand forecasting and inventory planning within the global supply chain. Fortunately, its technological sophistication has greatly evolved over the last few decades, as the global supply chain now see companies increasingly leveraging data and information to better forecast

From 1st November, the US will impose a 25% tariff on imported medium and heavy-duty trucks—part of a broader strategy by President Trump to use tariffs as a geopolitical tool. The rationale? Tariffs, he claims, help “prevent wars.” But the global reaction has been swift. Key allies including Mexico, Canada, Japan, and Germany are pushing back, raising concerns about supply chain [...] “Tariffs are back,” the real story is this: The people these tariffs were supposed to hurt aren’t feeling the pain. The ones getting crushed are the honest, smaller American businesses. results.title: Chain Reaction: US Tariffs and Global Supply Chains
results.content: Supply chains tend to move when goods can be manufactured in countries with lower “landed costs”—the cost of production plus shipping, customs duties, and insurance. Tariffs directly impact these calculations, which helps explain why US imports from China declined after the US imposed Section 301 tariffs on $550 billion of imports from China in 2017 (Figure 1). Transshipment played a role, but it only explains part of shifting trade flows over the period. Crucially, manufacturing capacity [...] Punitive targets: The administration will continue to use tariffs as a punitive tool, typified by US duties on India for Russian oil purchases and on Brazil for the prosecution of former president Jair Bolsonaro. [...] Resource constraints: Today, the US has higher tariffs on more products from more countries than at any point since the establishment of the modern global trade system. These have two deleterious effects: First, they increase inflation, which reduces total demand in the US, affecting company sales and increasing the cost of onshoring via higher labor, input, and production costs.
